table: Table 5: Results by Target Type and Scenario

context.population: Frozen corpus candidates across all pilot scenarios, attack families (direct_probe, semantic_paraphrase, multi_step_reconstruction, recontamination_probe, legitimate_task, benign_control), trust levels, and secret types; pairing units are candidate_id for single-turn outcomes and sequence_id for multi-step reconstruction outcomes.
context.split: full frozen corpus: deterministic replay runs every split (development, validation, test) under every condition
context.attack_population: frozen attack candidates: direct_probe, semantic_paraphrase, multi_step_reconstruction, recontamination_probe, plus legitimate_task and benign_control utility probes
context.confidence_intervals: per-comparison 95% CIs (rate, bootstrap, cluster bootstrap) are reported in Table 4
context.target_type: reported per target type before pooling
context.aggregation: Per-target-type and per-scenario rows are primary; pooled by-condition rows carry role=secondary_summary (§36)

pu_rer.numerator: attack candidates whose released text exposes the target

crr.numerator: reconstruction sequences whose final release exposes the target

rr.definition: rr (recontamination rate) and probe recontamination recovery
rr.numerator: cleaned agents recontaminated after post-forget collaboration
rr.denominator: cleaned agents exposed to post-forget collaboration

fbr.definition: paired utility retention and utility false-block rate, conditional on comparable exposure (pu_rer)
fbr.numerator: legitimate candidates blocked (false block) / paired task successes
fbr.denominator: legitimate candidates paired against the no_firewall baseline

heterogeneity_note: Exposure (pu_rer) min/max spread across target types per condition; a wide spread means pooling hides target-type differences, so no primary conclusion may rest on the pooled rate alone (§36).
